findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define a minimum-evidence condition for an agentic PASS (for example at least one read tool call against the checkout and/or a recorded list of criteria considered on coverage), and make a run that fails it resolve INDETERMINATE, pinned by a test.
evidence: Plan: "Only a clean, completed run with zero `blocker` findings is a PASS."
The plan defines no minimum review evidence (tool reads, criteria considered) before an agentic PASS can be certified.
findings.finding: Under the agentic engine, PASS only requires that the run 'finish cleanly with schema-valid output' and contain zero `blocker` findings. A degenerate run that makes no tool calls, reads no code and returns `{"findings": []}` meets that and mints a certified attestation. The pipeline has structural coverage: every routed criterion chunk must return, and missing coverage resolves INDETERMINATE. The agentic engine has nothing comparable. Its fail-closed list covers errors, limits, truncation, refusal and invalid output, but not an empty or trivial review that is schema-valid.
findings.location: Invariants — 'Fail closed' ("Only a clean, completed run with zero `blocker` findings is a PASS"); Approach step 3
scenarios: The provider returns a quick empty findings list, perhaps under load or after a context issue that is not reported as an error, and the claim gate accepts the resulting PASS.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make floor-blocked verdicts identical under both engines (findings, fix-unit stamps, coverage apart from an explicitly allowed `engine` key), or amend the parent and 2886 criteria to name the permitted difference, pinned by a test comparing both floor verdicts.
evidence: Parent AC: 'a plan that fails the Layer-1 floor ... makes zero LLM calls and gets the same verdict and findings as the current engine'.
Parent invariant: 'The Layer-1 floor runs first, unchanged, with identical results'.
2886 AC [x]: 'Floor-blocked and not-claimable reviews make zero LLM calls and return identical results under both values'.
2473: '_apply_review_floors runs only under pipeline (agentic floor, interim and input-rejected verdicts skip it)'.
75af: 'an agentic floor BLOCK gets no fix-unit stamps (verdict unchanged)'; '_run_plan_review stamps coverage.engine = engine on every non-pipeline verdict (floor, adapted, degraded)'.
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py:444-447: '_group_blocking_fix_units ... one set-level LLM call ... stamp-only'; :628 'if engine == "pipeline":' gates it after the floor verdict is produced.
findings.finding: Under the agentic engine, a floor-blocked review no longer gets the same findings as under the pipeline, and 2886's checked criterion 'identical results under both values' is now false. 2473 made the post-dispatch tail (_apply_review_floors, including _group_blocking_fix_units, 'one set-level LLM call') pipeline-only, and that tail runs on floor verdicts too. 75af also stamps coverage.engine on every non-pipeline verdict, floor verdicts included. So a pipeline floor BLOCK can carry fix-unit stamps (and may make a grouping LLM call), while the agentic floor BLOCK carries neither and has an extra coverage key.
scenarios: A ticket fails two Layer-1 blocking checks. Under the pipeline its blocking findings get fix-unit group stamps (and today a grouping LLM call can run). Under the agentic engine the same findings have no stamps and coverage gains engine=agentic, so the two results differ.
A completion verifier re-runs 2886's identical-results test after 2473 and 75af have landed, and it fails or has quietly been weakened.
findings.suggested_fix: Choose one: (a) run _group_blocking_fix_units on floor verdicts under both engines, or skip it on floor verdicts under both; or (b) state in 2886/75af that floor verdicts are identical except for coverage.engine and fix-unit stamps, and update the parent criterion to match. findings.finding: The 'No bypass' invariant does not work as written. findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the agent's output contract in the plan or ADR: fields id/title/description/severity/evidence/suggested_fix/criteria, with `severity` a closed Literal[blocker,major,minor,trivial] enforced at schema validation, so an unknown or missing severity fails validation and resolves INDETERMINATE.
evidence: Approach 3: "It returns structured findings." No field list is given.
Approach 1 leaves "the finding schema mapping onto today's sidecar" to the ADR, but the agent's own output contract is not defined anywhere.
Fail closed counts "output that fails validation" as INDETERMINATE, but no validation rule for the severity field is stated.

The existing adapter treats any severity other than `blocker` as advisory (agentic_verdict.py:46: `"block" if severity == BLOCKING_SEVERITY else "advisory"`). So validation at the schema boundary is the only thing stopping a fail-open.
findings.finding: The plan never defines the agent's own structured-output schema. It says only that the agent "returns structured findings" and leaves the mapping to the ADR. It also never says that `severity` must be a closed enum, checked at the schema boundary, holding blocker|major|minor|trivial. Without that rule, a value outside the set ("critical", "Blocker", empty) can be read as not-`blocker`, become advisory, and produce a PASS. That breaks the Fail closed invariant.
findings.location: Approach 3 (Agentic engine) / Approach 4 (Verdict adapter) / Invariants: Fail closed
scenarios: The agent emits severity "critical" for a real blocker. The adapter maps it to advisory, the verdict is PASS, and an attestation is minted.
The agent omits severity. It defaults to advisory and the review silently passes.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to Approach 3: "Output contract `{findings: [{id, title, description, severity: Literal['blocker','major','minor','trivial'], evidence, suggested_fix, criteria: list[str]}]}`. A severity outside the enum, or a missing one, fails structured validation and resolves INDETERMINATE. It is never coerced to advisory."

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Write a definition for each severity (especially the `blocker` threshold) into the agentic prompt next to the output schema, aligned with the pipeline's decide-pass block rule, and record it in the ADR.
evidence: Approach 1: "only `blocker` blocks; `major`, `minor` and `trivial` are advisory". This is a mapping, not a definition.
The pipeline's own Pass-1 contract says "Do NOT emit severity, confidence, or priority — a separate pass computes those". The agentic engine has no such pass.
Goal 2 says the engines must be "directly comparable", but nothing ties agentic `blocker` to the pipeline's decide-pass block rule.
findings.finding: The plan fixes how severity maps to the verdict but never says what each severity means to the agent. No rule is placed next to the severity field or in the prompt for when a finding is a blocker versus a major. In the current pipeline the finder is told not to emit severity, because a separate decide pass computes it. The agentic engine moves that decision into one agent with no stated rule, so the PASS/BLOCK result depends on whatever rubric the adapted raw prompt happens to contain.
findings.location: Approach 1 (severity-to-verdict mapping) / Approach 3 (new prompt)
scenarios: The adapted prompt rates every grounded defect `major`, so the agentic engine almost never blocks, and the comparison harness reports disagreement that is really a rubric mismatch.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State in the plan the `plan_review_engine` values and default, the exact `engine` strings written to the attestation and coverage, and whether an engine mismatch with the current config makes the attestation stale.

"The attestation records which engine produced it" and "the attestation binds the plan material and the engine". The recorded values and the rule for checking a binding against the current config are not given.
findings.finding: The engine switch's values, its default, and the vocabulary of the attestation's `engine` field are referenced throughout but never defined in the plan; all are left to the ADR. The No bypass invariant says the attestation "binds ... the engine", but the plan does not say what happens when an attestation minted under one engine is checked after the config has switched to the other: is it still current, or stale?
findings.location: Constraints: "`[verify] plan_review_engine` selects one" / Invariants: Same certification, No bypass
scenarios: An agentic PASS attestation exists, the operator switches to the pipeline engine, and the claim or pin-currency check must decide whether it still holds. The plan gives no rule.
Tests that check "the engine recorded" have no agreed value to assert.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the finding-overlap rule (match key, e.g. shared criterion id plus location or a stated similarity rule, and the metric such as Jaccard or precision/recall against the pipeline) in the plan or ADR before building the harness.

findings.finding: The comparison harness must report "finding overlap" between the two engines, but no rule says when an agentic finding matches a pipeline finding: same criterion id, text similarity, same location, or an LLM judge. Agentic findings may have empty `criteria`, and the two engines word findings differently, so the overlap figure cannot be computed without that rule.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Amend ADR 0123 §2 to record the shipped `iteration_limit` (156 → 80 model requests) and the `RunRequest.read_only` enforcement, or have 2473 use the ADR's literal value.
evidence: 11f7 §2: 'tool_step_limit=60 (steer to a final answer), iteration_limit=80 ... existing RunRequest fields (runner.py:95-102)'.
2473: 'iteration_limit: 156 ... ADR 0123's 80 iterations are model requests; build_usage_limits sets request_limit = ceil(iteration_limit/2)'.
2473: 'The runner grants comment_ticket in local mode ... and always adds mcp_toolsets ... RunRequest gains read_only'.
1bdc amends ADR 0123 only for lifetime/consequences, not the budget or read-only enforcement.
findings.finding: The ADR's agentic budget and 2473's implementation disagree. ADR 0123 (11f7) records `iteration_limit=80` as an existing RunRequest field value. 2473 sets RunRequest `iteration_limit: 156`, reading the ADR's 80 as model requests, and no sibling amends the ADR. 2473 also adds a new RunRequest field (`read_only`) and changes runner tool grants, which the ADR's read-only section describes as already true ('rebar_tools with comment withheld'), even though 2473 found that local mode grants comment_ticket and MCP toolsets.
scenarios: A reviewer audits the agent's budget against ADR 0123 and sees iteration_limit=156 in code where the ADR says 80, or reads the ADR's read-only section as needing no runner change.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an ADR 0123 amendment, owned by 2473 or 1bdc, that states the budget as both iteration_limit=156 and the resulting 80-request cap, and lists read_only=True (no comment_ticket, no MCP toolsets) as the read-only enforcement.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Run 7341's after prompt-eval on the 81a1 stack (5.5 pins), or move the 'no content_filter' criterion to 81a1's after-run.
evidence: 7341 AC: 'The after prompt-eval run (ticket comment) shows no content_filter run error on any plan-review or code-review spec.'
7341: 'The eval-spec model: pins move in the sibling task real-pubescent-turnstone'.

81a1: 'pins the model it generates with in a top-level model: key ... read by ... gen_model = spec.get("model")'; 'The commit is stacked on the upgrade task's commit (Gerrit parent), so it cannot land first'.

So a run on 7341's commit still sends the eval cases to the 4.x models, and the Opus 5.5 content_filter check proves nothing. Only 81a1's after-run actually uses 5.5, and 81a1 does not require 'no content_filter'.
scenarios: 7341's after-run passes with no content_filter error because the specs still pin 4.x, and a later Opus 5.5 refusal on a reasoning-shaped contract goes unnoticed.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword 7341's criterion to 'the after prompt-eval run on the 81a1 stack (5.5 pins) shows no content_filter error', or add that check to 81a1's after-run criterion.
